title: The Broken Choir Again
premise: Ada Montrose poisons herself daily by profession and keeps double ledgers for the Choir, a guild that trades in impossible things—bottled grief, borrowed luck, second chances. When the old gods resume answering prayers, every debt in her ledgers comes due at once, including the soul of her dead sister, sold decades ago to the court beneath the mountain. As the usurper's armies march on the free cities, Ada must abandon the invisibility she has cultivated all her life, rally the Choir's scattered debtors, and descend to bargain with a king who collects souls as interest. She wins her sister back not by force but by proving the court's own ledger fraudulent—an act of justice outside any law—and returns to a city on fire, choosing at last to stand visible among the people who need her.
about_author: Emrys Iversen is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing medieval guild records before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about ordinary people who keep extraordinary books.

chapters.title: The Taster's Portion
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. We meet her mid-ritual: swallowing arsenic-laced honey cake for the magistrate's table while memorizing the Choir's ledger by candlelight. A prayer whispered over dinner is answered aloud—the first time in three hundred years. Emotional beat: quiet dread beneath routine; the world has shifted and no one else noticed.

chapters.title: Entries Outstanding
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The old gods' return activates dormant contracts; debtors flood the guildhouse demanding miracles or mercy. Ada discovers one entry in her late mother's hand: 'One soul, Montrose line, sold to the Undercourt.' Emotional beat: betrayal braided with grief—her family's history was a transaction she never consented to.

chapters.title: The Usurper's Summons
chapters.summary: Dual POV: Ada and Captain Veyra, the usurper's inquisitor. The usurper demands the Choir's ledgers as proof the free cities traffic with forbidden gods. Veyra, pragmatic and weary, suspects the summons is a trap for her too. Emotional beat: two women on collision course, each serving systems that would discard them.

chapters.title: Debtors' Vigil
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The Choir scatters; its master flees, leaving Ada the ledgers and the blame. She convenes the debtors—a smuggler, a rain-priestess, a man owed his own name—and offers them a choice: run, or help her raid the Undercourt. Emotional beat: reluctant belonging; Ada learns she has been someone's anchor without knowing it.

chapters.title: What the Mountain Owes
chapters.summary: Veyra's POV. Interrogating the guildmaster's abandoned records, Veyra finds the same Montrose entry—and evidence the usurper's own crown was purchased from the Undercourt with souls as collateral. Emotional beat: disillusionment; her loyalty cracks as she realizes the law she enforces is itself an unpaid debt.

chapters.title: Descent
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Guided by the rain-priestess through drowned mine-shafts, Ada reaches the court beneath the mountain, where the Soul-King weighs petitioners like coin. She offers her taster's immunity—her body, proof against every poison—as collateral for her sister's soul. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into audacity; invisible Ada makes herself the prize.

chapters.title: The Fraudulent Ledger
chapters.summary: Ada's POV, with the Soul-King. Auditing the Undercourt's own accounts, Ada proves her sister's contract was void—signed by a mother who had already pawned that soul elsewhere, meaning the court holds stolen goods. The Soul-King, bound by his own bookkeeping, must release her. Emotional beat: triumph of precision over power; justice rendered by arithmetic.

chapters.title: Armies at the Gates
chapters.summary: Dual POV. The usurper's vanguard breaches the free cities; Veyra, ordered to burn the guildhouse, instead burns the usurper's collateral receipts and defects. Ada surfaces from the mountain into smoke, carrying her sister's soul in a lead vial. Emotional beat: convergence; both women choose treason in the same hour, independently.

chapters.title: The Broken Choir Sings
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. At the burning city's heart, Ada releases her sister's soul before the assembled crowd—and the old gods answer publicly, restoring the Choir as something new: not a guild of debts but a court of appeals where the powerless are heard. Veyra stands witness against the usurper. Emotional beat: catharsis; invisibility ends in chorus.

chapters.title: A New Entry
chapters.summary: Ada's POV, epilogue. Months later, Ada writes the first page of a fresh ledger—not of what people owe, but of what they are owed. Her sister, half-real and learning to be alive again, asks what Ada will write first. Emotional beat: tender resolution; inheritance transformed from burden into promise.
